About me

I'm a mechanical engineering student at the American University of Beirut. I like ideas that turn into things, and I'm usually the one pushing a team from a sketch to a working prototype.

Hands-on work is where I think best. I build it, test it, break it and fix it again. That loop is the part I enjoy most.

I'm family-first, a loyal friend, and busy most of the time, which suits me. I've had some hard years, and I still find a way to keep going. People tell me I'm a sunshine, and I try to get the team to do its best.

Outside the workshop I write and draw now and then, but engineering takes most of my time.

— Ayda

Experience logbook

  1. 01

    AUB Super Mileage Team

    Vehicle restoration

    Contributing to the restoration of the team's 2019 car, including work around the motor, brakes, wheels, steering and vehicle components. Prototyped a 3D-printed steering attachment through the Red Room.

  2. 02

    Baja SAE

    Team development · vehicle design

    Helping establish a new Baja SAE team and exploring early powertrain and drivetrain concepts, with attention to off-road capability and endurance reliability.

  3. 03

    AUB Red Room · JEDI

    Makerspace · prototyping

    Hands-on work with 3D modelling, printing workflows, physical assembly, prototyping and electronics in student engineering projects.

  4. 04

    ASME AUB

    Secretary

    Documentation, meeting minutes, archives and notices, plus the organizational follow-up that helps the student chapter run smoothly.

  5. 05

    Lebanese Aerospace and Automotive Society (LAAS)

    Public relations officer

    Outreach and communication for the society's aerospace and automotive engineering activities.

  6. 06

    Scouting · Cheftaine, Meute Akela

    Youth leadership

    Planning activities and group experiences that build teamwork, responsibility, creativity and outdoor skills.

04

Motorsports first

Motorsports is the part of engineering that pulls me in most. I want to work on cars that have to finish, not just look fast: the drivetrain, the steering, the brakes, and the parts that have to survive a long race.

That's why I've been on the Super Mileage restoration and the Baja SAE team. Both put a real car in front of me, and both have taught me more than a textbook could.

Open to motorsports teams and internships.
